newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX wants to regain regional leadership.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX wants to regain regional leadership.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) required an easier regulatory and taxation system if it hoped to regain its position as the dominant equities market in the Southeast Asia/Pacific region, ASX managing director Dick Humphry said.

Humphry told the Committee for Economic Development of Australia that five years ago the Australian market was capitalised at US$130 billion compared with a combined capitalisation of US$230 billion for Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.
"In other words, it had 36 percent of the significant regional market. Today, our share is down to 23 percent, and falling," he said.

"While we have doubled our market size in five years, which is respectable enough in itself, Hong Kong has tripled, Malaysia and Singapore have quadrupled and Thailand has quintupled. Admittedly they were starting from smaller bases and had faster-growing economies but the difference is still startling."
Humphry said the ASX believed Australian capital markets and companies were over-regulated and called on the government to redraft and simplify the governing Corporations Law.
He also said stamp duty on share market transactions should be reduced and the bias against foreign companies evident in the dividend imputation system should be examined.
